stem: Anaya keeps dry chana seeds in a jar. She later places some on moist cotton, and they sprout into seedlings.

parts.text: How should Anaya classify a seed after considering germination?

options.text: Living, because under suitable conditions it can germinate into a young plant.
Non-living whenever it is dry and has not yet sprouted.
Living even if conditions stay unsuitable and it never sprouts.
Non-living, like a wooden pencil that came from a tree.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A seed connects to living processes because favourable conditions let it germinate and grow into a young plant.

teacher.key_rationale: A seed is classed with living things because under suitable conditions it germinates into a young plant. Dry appearance alone does not make it non-living, unsuitable conditions are not ignored, and a pencil is a non-living contrast.
